textbookBox.concept: A shape has a line of symmetry if folding along the line makes both halves match exactly. This is reflection symmetry.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A shape has a line of symmetry if folding along the line makes both halves match exactly. This is reflection symmetry.
beats.speakEn: A shape has a line of symmetry if folding along the line makes both halves match exactly. This is reflection symmetry.

beats.en: The letter A has a vertical line of symmetry. To cut it: fold the paper in half, draw half of A along the fold, cut along the outline, and open it to see a full A.
beats.speakEn: The letter A has a vertical line of symmetry. To cut it: fold the paper in half, draw half of A along the fold, cut along the outline, and open it to see a full A.

type: Key Concept: A shape has a line of symmetry if folding along the line makes both halves match exactly.
Rule: The letter A has a vertical line of symmetry.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 5 maths · Symmetrical Designs · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: The letter H has two lines of symmetry, one vertical and one horizontal. Fold the paper into four (one-fourth), draw one fourth of H, cut and open.

beats.en: The letter H has two lines of symmetry, one vertical and one horizontal. Fold the paper into four (one-fourth), draw one fourth of H, cut and open.
beats.speakEn: The letter H has two lines of symmetry, one vertical and one horizontal. Fold the paper into four (one-fourth), draw one fourth of H, cut and open.

beats.en: Now test the letters E N X T K V O. Horizontal line of symmetry: E, X, K, O. Vertical line: T, X, V, O. Both lines: X and O. N has no line of symmetry.
